pass1.sentence: its concentration can climb steeply during a severe infection
Starts to rise within hours of a trigger, peaks within a day or two and falls quickly once the trigger resolves.
pass1.note: Reviews: begins to rise 6-12 h, peaks about 48 h, half-life about 19 h. Numbers softened to words.

pass1.sentence: Very high levels suggest bacterial infection or major inflammation; mild elevations are common and non-specific.
pass1.note: Review: levels as high as 400 mg/L usually only in severe bacterial infection or sepsis; '100 mg/L' and 'in the hundreds' not defined as a standard band in any retrieved page.

pass1.sentence: For adults with a suspected lower respiratory tract infection, NICE uses a point-of-care CRP below 20 mg/L, 20 to 100 mg/L and above 100 mg/L to help decide whether to offer antibiotics.
pass1.note: NG237: offer immediately if >100; consider back-up/delayed prescription 20-100; do not routinely offer <20.

pass1.sentence: Mildly raised CRP (a small rise above the laboratory's reference limit)
pass1.note: 'roughly 5-20 mg/L': no retrieved page defines a mild band; one hospital lists 0-5, another 'normal under 10', so the number was removed.
